source_refs.note: Book p. 5: 1.3.1 Fundamental Transcendental Functions (definition with standard examples)

blocks.text: Pichle section mein humne functions ko algebraic aur transcendental mein baanta. Ab transcendental family ke andar bhi do hisse hain: fundamental (buniyadi) aur non-fundamental. Is chhote se subtopic mein hum buniyadi wale dekhenge, kyun ke baqi sab inhi se bante hain.

Kitab ki definition: fundamental transcendental functions woh aam istemal hone wale standard transcendental functions hain jaise \(y = a^{x}\ (a > 0, a \ne 1)\), \(y = \ln x\), \(y = \sin x\), \(y = \sin^{-1} x\). Yeh zyada complex (pecheeda) transcendental functions ki buniyad (base) banate hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Inhein Lego ke bunyadi blocks samjhiye. Jaise chand bunyadi blocks se poora ghar ban jata hai, waise hi in chand standard functions ko jor kar, ek doosre ke andar daal kar (composition), ya shift kar ke baqi tamam complex transcendental functions bante hain. Har fundamental function ek family se talluq rakhta hai, neeche table dekhiye:

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Ab sawal yeh hai ke \(y = a^{x}\) ke saath shartein \(a > 0\) aur \(a \ne 1\) kyun lagayi gayi hain? Teen surtein dekhiye:
Agar \(a = 1\) ho to har \(x\) ke liye \(1^{x} = 1\). Yeh to ek constant function ban gaya, jo algebraic hai, transcendental nahin. Graph bas ek seedhi horizontal line hoga.
Agar \(a < 0\) ho, maslan \(a = -4\), to \((-4)^{1/2} = \sqrt{-4}\) koi real number nahin. Yani \(a^{x}\) har real \(x\) ke liye defined hi nahin.
Agar \(a = 0\) ho to \(0^{x}\) \(x \le 0\) ke liye undefined hai (jaise \(0^{-1} = \frac{1}{0}\), aur zero se taqseem mumkin nahin).
Is liye sirf woh base jo positive ho aur 1 na ho, sahi exponential function deta hai. Is ki tafseel hum 1.4 mein parhenge.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Kya \(y = 5^{x}\) fundamental transcendental function hai? Aur \(y = 1^{x}\)?
Jawab: \(5^{x}\) haan, kyun ke \(a = 5 > 0\) aur \(5 \ne 1\). Lekin \(1^{x} = 1\) sirf constant hai, is liye exponential function nahin.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Fundamental transcendental functions standard functions hain: \(a^{x}\ (a > 0, a \ne 1)\), \(\ln x\), \(\sin x\), \(\sin^{-1} x\) aur in ki families.
2. Inhi se zyada complex transcendental functions bante hain (agla subtopic).
3. \(y = a^{x}\) mein base ki shartein: \(a > 0\) aur \(a \ne 1\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(1^{x}\) ko exponential function samajhna; yeh to hamesha 1 hai, constant function.
2. \((-2)^{x}\) ko exponential function likhna; yeh \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) jaisi values par defined hi nahin.
3. Yeh samajhna ke jis function mein bhi \(\sin\) ya \(\ln\) aa jaye woh fundamental hai. \(\sin x + \ln x\) do functions ka jor hai, is liye non-fundamental hai (1.3.2 dekhiye).
